evidence.reasoning:
Source of dissect_extended_bootstrap_register shows unconditional writes:
  gvcp_register_number[gvcp_register_count] = addr;
  gvcp_register_value[gvcp_register_count++] = value;
with no bounds check on gvcp_register_count. Same pattern exists in dissect_register.

However, tool check_reachability reports dissect_extended_bootstrap_register is NOT in the fuzzer call graph (reachable:false). So the specific claimed site cannot be exercised by the fuzzer as configured.

I did not locate the definitions/sizes of gvcp_register_number/value or gvcp_register_count via read_function (they are globals, not functions), so I cannot confirm the array bounds, but the pattern is a classic potential global OOB if gvcp_register_count can exceed the array length. No evidence of any clamp/guard in the shown functions.

No reach_probe was run, so there is no grounded proof of an ASan global-buffer-overflow crash in this harness.
evidence.corrected_description: Potential global-buffer-overflow: dissect_register (and dissect_extended_bootstrap_register, if reachable) append to global arrays gvcp_register_number/value using gvcp_register_count++ without any bounds check; if gvcp_register_count can exceed the arrays' fixed size, writes go out of bounds.
evidence.control_flow_to_bug: From handler_gvcp -> dissect_gvcp -> (command parsing) -> register-dissection loop(s) calling dissect_register repeatedly; each call increments gvcp_register_count and writes gvcp_register_number/value at that index. If enough register entries are processed in one conversation/transaction without resetting gvcp_register_count, it can exceed the global array capacity and write past the end. (dissect_extended_bootstrap_register was reported unreachable in this harness.)

full_messages.content:
You are a vulnerability verifier. All candidate functions are already
reachable from the fuzzer — do NOT re-litigate reachability as pass/fail. Your job
is to gather EVIDENCE about whether the reached code actually contains a
crashing memory-safety bug of the stated type, then submit it.

Gather evidence with the tools:
- read_function(name): read the real source.
- check_reachability(function_name): confirm the call graph (depth, direct/indirect).
- reach_probe(generator_code, target): write Python `def generate()->bytes` that
  produces an input aiming to REACH `target` (a function name or "file.c:LINE").
  It runs the input on the real ASan binary under gdb and tells you whether the
  target was reached and whether it crashed. A crash is proof; a reach grounds
  your judgment. Only a real crash or reach can raise the score above the ceiling —
  you cannot assert a high score from reading alone.
- submit_evidence(...): report your structured findings (see its schema). Call it
  once, last.

Two of the fields are NOT about scoring — they correct the SP for the downstream
PoV stage, and you are the right one to write them because you just read the real
code (and maybe ran a reach_probe):
- corrected_description: if the SP's stated bug type/description is wrong or
  imprecise given the real code, write the accurate one (else restate it).
- control_flow_to_bug: the real path from the fuzzer entry to the crash site — the
  key functions, branches, and conditions that must hold to trigger it.

Do NOT pass things "when in doubt". Report what the evidence shows. Absence of a
crash is not proof of safety; a proven clamp/guard on the tainted value IS
disconfirming.

Verify this suspicious point.

Fuzzer: handler_gvcp   Sanitizer: address
Function: dissect_extended_bootstrap_register
Claimed bug type: global-buffer-overflow
Suspicious-point description (from the finder — may be imprecise): `gvcp_register_number[gvcp_register_count] = addr; gvcp_register_value[gvcp_register_count++] = value;` index global arrays by a monotonically increasing `gvcp_register_count` that is never bounds-checked, so a packet with enough register writes overflows the global arrays.

Control flow to the bug:
  - handler_gvcp writes a sequence of registers
  - each dissect_register/dissect_extended_bootstrap_register does gvcp_register_*[gvcp_register_count++]
  - gvcp_register_count exceeds the global array size -> global-buffer-overflow

The function is reachable (confirm with check_reachability if useful).

Read the function, judge whether a fuzzer input can drive a global-buffer-overflow
there, optionally reach_probe a candidate input to ground it, then submit_evidence.
